newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh gas fire may take month to put out.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh gas fire may take month to put out.

text.p: Bangladesh Energy Minister Nooruddin Khan said on Thursday foreign experts might take about a month to extinguish a gas field fire that has endangered part of a rain forest and tea gardens in the country's northeast.
"Although it all depends on what method they (experts) would use, the likely time limit (for extinguishing the fire fully) is one month," Khan told Reuters.
He said experts from Singapore and the United States had not yet decided how to tame the fire that engulfed the gas field at Magurchhara in Maulavi Bazar district early on Sunday.
The fire ignited when a rig drilled by the U.S. oil firm Occidental Petroleum Corp hit a "trap gas" layer.
The experts went to work after two plane loads of fire fighting equipment arrived from overseas on Wednesday, ministry officials said.
The fire badly damaged an estimated 200 acres (80 hectares) of the sourrounding forest, and partially burnt three tea gardens and plantations farmed by tribal Khasia villagers.
Forest authorities have estimated losses at around two billion taka ($45 million) and said on Wednesday they would ask for compensation from Occidental.
The blaze also damaged a railway track, forcing suspension of rail traffic between the capital Dhaka and northeastern districts.
Khan said his ministry would back compensation claims by the forest department, railway and any other affected firm or groups.
However he ruled out imposing stricter safety rules on the U.S. firm when it resumes exploration.
"They are a big name in the energy world, have enormous expertise. They understand safety better than us," he said, adding that Occidental was following international drilling regulations.
Occidental is drilling for gas and oil in some 35 fields in different countries.

Khan allayed fears of a loss of gas reserves in the field, saying the extractable gas was at a depth of 3,700 metres (12,100 feet) while the layer from where the gas was blowing out was at 840 metres (2,755 feet).
The minsiter said Occidental would resume drilling in the field at a different site by the end of July.

"They said their rigs will be in place by the middle of July and (will) start drilling by the month end. They said they would put up three rigs simultaneously to make up the time lost by the accident."
Sunday's fire destroyed the rig and other equipment.
Occidental, which owns rights to explore for hydrocarbons in the entire Sylhet region, plans to spend $100 million on exploration in the area.
